messages:
maria: kicking off a short thread — I sketched a new synthetic traffic generator concept I'm calling 'fractal spike ensemble' (FSE). goal: reproduce long-tailed session arrivals + nested microbursts so we can stress kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV warmup patterns in a single workload. wanna run this by the runtime folks and get quick feedback.

raj: love the name :grin: high-level — how does FSE differ from the existing surge/poisson generators?

maria: two main diffs: (1) hierarchical arrival process: a heavy-tailed session inter-arrival (Pareto-like) creates user sessions; within each session we spawn self-similar ON/OFF substreams to produce microbursts; (2) token/len distribution coupling so long responses coincide with bursts (exposes kv cache and kernel path stress).

devon: that coupling is key. we often see kernels switch when seq_len > 1024 and that plus batching cause tail latency spikes. if bursts push many long requests at once, batching heuristics either overbatch (higher latency) or underbatch (lower throughput).

ingrid: can you paste the proto config? even a small example helps reproduce.

maria: sure — here's the proto snippet I'm iterating on:

```
# fractal_spike_ensemble config (YAML-like)
baseline: 
  qps: 20
  arrival: poisson

sessions:
  distribution: pareto
  shape: 1.7  # heavy tail for session arrivals
  mean_duration: 300s

within_session:
  stream_type: on_off_self_similar
  hurst: 0.75  # controls burstiness
  on_mean: 2s
  off_mean: 10s
  microburst_multiplier: [1, 5, 20]  # mix of small/med/large bursts

response_profile:
  p_long: 0.12  # 12% long responses
  long_len_dist: pareto(scale=512, shape=1.5)
  short_len_dist: normal(mean=64, sd=16)

kv_warmup:
  strategy: progressive_prefix_cache
  ramp_up_window: 45s
  prefetch_rate: 0.3  # fraction of requests that prefetch KV entries
```

maria: note: the progressive_prefix_cache tries to emulate real clients that tend to request earlier tokens first, so KV hit-rate ramps during a session rather than instant warm cache.

kai: interesting. two quick worries: (A) reproducibility — seeds and deterministic stream generation are essential for apples-to-apples between kernels. (B) measurement windows: need to capture tail over long enough time (minutes) because Pareto sessions produce rare huge spikes.

sophie: on the KV side, the prefetch_rate knob is very useful. it lets us test 'cold prefix' vs 'warm prefix' scenarios. could we add a variant that forces random-token access to stress KV randomness?

maria: yes — plus a mode where within_session long requests have high entropy prompts so KV caches see low locality. that should regress quantized kernels that assume high KV locality.

perf-bot: perf summary (quick run): FSE small-scale run (seed=42, 5m) -> mean QPS 22, p95 latency 312ms, p99 latency 1.9s, KV hit-rate ramped 18% -> 72% over session windows.

raj: thanks perf-bot. p99 near 2s is actionable. can we tag which kernel was selected during the p99 spikes? we need a timeline mapping kernel variant -> latency to find mis-selection events.

devon: propose adding inline trace points to the generator that emit events: `kernel_hint`, `batch_size`, `kv_hit_estimate` on every request. then in the prod harness we can join traces with runtime's kernel-selection logs. minimal overhead if we sample at 1%.

ingrid: +1. also add a 'ramp jitter' param for QPS ramps so we avoid perfectly deterministic ramps causing synchronized behavior with autoscaler/pacing. small random jitter breaks lockstep.

maria: action items: (1) i'll add seeds + deterministic mode + ramp_jitter (2) add kernel_hint + batch_size sampling (3) create two variants: high-locality and low-locality KV profiles (4) run a cross-kernel apples-to-apples with same seed and attach trace mapping. will post results.

kai: when you run, include a baseline with continuous batching disabled to measure the batching heuristic cost. also try quantized kernel and fp16 kernel.

perf-bot: scheduled job: /runs/fse/2024-06-12/seed-42 created. will push quick CSV and traces to /tmp/perf-fse-20240612.zip when complete.

maria: great — thanks everyone. i'll drop the first reproducible run in this thread when done. any other quick asks before I run?

raj: maybe add an explicit 'canary session' flag that generates a massive single session (very low prob) so we can validate graceful fallback and model-variant routing under catastrophic load.

maria: added to todo. :thumbsup:

kai: awesome. if we see persistent p99 > 1s on quantized path, we'll open a perf-regression issue and include the FSE replay.

maria: cool — thanks all.
